name: MATHQA
intro: MathQA 将 AQuA-RAT 英文多项选择数学文字题与可执行运算程序对齐。论文表 1 报告 37,259 题和 58 种运算；官方仓库固定提交 4f958013 的公开核心 train/dev/test 实际合计 37,297 题，因此详情页明确区分论文清单与发布清单。
org: University of Washington, Allen Institute for AI
build_method: AQuA-RAT 筛选, 动态众包程序标注, 2/3 多人验证, 近重复扩展
task_type: 数学文字题, 程序生成
eval_feature: 论文 Seq2prog/Seq2prog+cat：Python OpenNMT 两层 LSTM（hidden 100，Adam 0.001），测试时仅以题目文本预测程序，束大小 100；执行后匹配选项；官方模型检查点与评测器代码未发布
scale: 论文表 1：37,259 题；官方固定版本核心拆分：29,837 train + 4,475 dev + 2,985 test = 37,297，另有 604 题 challenge_test
build_method_en: AQuA-RAT Screening, Dynamic Crowdsourced Program Annotation, 2-of-3 Validation, Near-duplicate Expansion
eval_feature_en: Paper Seq2prog/Seq2prog+cat: two-layer Python OpenNMT LSTM (hidden 100, Adam 0.001), predict from problem text only at test time with beam size 100, execute, then map to an option; no official checkpoint or evaluator code is released
intro_en: MathQA aligns English multiple-choice math word problems from AQuA-RAT with executable operation programs. Paper Table 1 reports 37,259 problems and 58 operations, while the public core train/dev/test files at official commit 4f958013 contain 37,297 records; this page keeps the paper and release inventories distinct.
scale_en: Paper Table 1: 37,259; pinned official core: 29,837 train + 4,475 dev + 2,985 test = 37,297, plus 604 separate challenge_test records

drawio_review_note: Evidence boundary: MathQA (NAACL 2019 / ACL Anthology N19-1245), official math-QA/math-QA commit 4f958013c164a40745a5b771dfb005df308deb4a (2019-06-02), its MathQA.zip, and AllenAI loader/card commit c4f1cc784c04c4957b50c97858f23893b633eea6 (2024-01-18). The AllenAI revision pins the loader and card, but its loader still downloads an unversioned project URL; the official repository commit and ZIP are therefore the data evidence. The paper screens AQuA-RAT, defines 58 operations and six term-frequency categories, uses a dynamic Figure Eight interface with valid-argument hints and step execution, applies submission and worker-quality gates, accepts alignment with at least two of three votes, expands near-duplicates at a four-word Levenshtein threshold, and reports 37,259 items with an 80/12/8 random split. The paper reports 94.64% crowd validation accuracy and a 500-item expert evaluation with 92% validity and 87% agreement; it does not state that the expert evaluation filtered the release. Automatically derived rationale programs were excluded after only 61% passed validation. The pinned official ZIP instead contains 29,837 train + 4,475 dev + 2,985 test = 37,297 core records, plus 604 challenge_test records; operation_list.txt has 78 nonempty rows while 53 operation names occur in released formulas. Every public test row includes Problem, Rationale, options, correct, annotated_formula, linear_formula, and category, so there are no hidden official test labels. The paper trains Seq2prog and category-constrained Seq2prog+cat with the official Python OpenNMT implementation, a two-layer LSTM encoder-decoder with hidden size 100 and Adam learning rate 0.001. At test time the model receives problem text only, beam-decodes 100 programs, executes them sequentially, maps numeric results to answer options, and reports answer accuracy (51.9% / 54.2%; random 20.0%). The pinned project links a static Main MathQA Challenge leaderboard table, including category-level results, but provides no live submission or versioned-board interface. The project does not release annotation scripts, an official model checkpoint, evaluator code, the worker threshold, or the numeric option-matching threshold; the paper/release count and operation-list differences are therefore shown rather than reconciled.
